encounters.cc: Acute weakness and numbness in the right upper extremity following overhead lifting of heavy boxes two weeks ago, with difficulty gripping objects.

lines: Acute weakness and numbness in the right upper extremity following overhead lifting of heavy boxes two weeks ago, with difficulty gripping objects.

The patient returns to the emergency department with recurrent upper extremity symptoms, having previously presented to Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation in January 2020 with similar complaints affecting the left arm.
He has a known history of cervical spondylosis with multilevel degenerative disc disease at C5-C6 and C6-C7.
He works as a warehouse loader and states that the current symptoms began two weeks ago after lifting several heavy boxes overhead.
He reports that the weakness seems to be worse when gripping objects tightly or pushing open doors.
He also describes a tingling sensation that radiates from his shoulder down the posterior aspect of the arm and forearm, and into the middle finger.
The symptoms worsen when he tilts his head to the right or looks upward for prolonged periods.
